arxiv-2003-01025.title: Dynamic Queue-Jump Lane for Emergency Vehicles under Partially Connected Settings: A Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach Journal: Transportation Research Part C
arxiv-2003-01025.creator: Haoran Su, Kejian Shi, Joseph. Y.J. Chow, Li Jin
arxiv-2003-01025.description: Abstract Emergency vehicle (EMV) service is a key function of cities and is exceedingly challenging due to urban traffic congestion. A main reason behind EMV service delay is the lack of communication and cooperation between vehicles blocking EMVs. In this paper, we study the improvement of EMV service under V2X connectivity.

arxiv-2010-13475.title: On the Non-Commuting Graph of the Group U 6 ​ n U_{6n}
arxiv-2010-13475.creator: Sanhan Khasraw, C.H. Jaf, Nor Haniza Sarmin, Ibrahim Gambo
arxiv-2010-13475.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Sanhan Khasraw, C.H. Jaf, Nor Haniza Sarmin, Ibrahim Gambo. A non-commuting graph of a finite group G G is a graph whose vertices are non-central elements of G G and two vertices are adjacent if they don’t commute in G G . In this paper, we study the non-commuting graph of the group U 6 ​ n U_{6n} and explore some of its properties including the independent number, clique and chromatic numbers.

arxiv-2101-00454.title: Mining the online infosphere: A survey Thanks: The first nine authors have been arranged based on family names and have equal contributions.
arxiv-2101-00454.creator: Sayantan Adak, Souvic Chakraborty, Paramtia Das, Mithun Das, Abhisek Dash, Rima Hazra, Binny Mathew, Punyajoy Saha, Soumya Sarkar, Animesh Mukherjee
arxiv-2101-00454.description: Abstract The evolution of AI-based system and applications had pervaded everyday life to make decisions that have momentous impact on individuals and society. With the staggering growth of online data, often termed as the Online Infosphere it has become paramount to monitor the infosphere to ensure social good as the AI-based decisions are severely dependant on it.

arxiv-2102-09964.title: Temporal Gaussian Process Regression in Logarithmic Time
arxiv-2102-09964.creator: Adrien Corenflos, Zheng Zhao, Simo Särkkä
arxiv-2102-09964.description: Abstract The aim of this article is to present a novel parallelization method for temporal Gaussian process (GP) regression problems. The method allows for solving GP regression problems in logarithmic O ⁡ ( log ⁡ N ) O(\log N) time, where N N is the number of time steps.

arxiv-2207-08554.title: Regressive versions of Hindman’s Theorem
arxiv-2207-08554.creator: Lorenzo Carlucci, Leonardo Mainardi
arxiv-2207-08554.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Lorenzo Carlucci, Leonardo Mainardi. When the Canonical Ramsey’s Theorem by Erdős and Rado is applied to regressive functions, one obtains the Regressive Ramsey’s Theorem by Kanamori and McAloon. Taylor proved a “canonical” version of Hindman’s Theorem, analogous to the Canonical Ramsey’s Theorem.

arxiv-2208-11076.title: The JADE Experiment at the PETRA e + ​ e − e^{+}e^{-} collider - history, achievements and revival
arxiv-2208-11076.creator: S. Bethke, A. Wagner
arxiv-2208-11076.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by S. Bethke, A. Wagner. The JADE experiment was one of five large detector systems taking data at the electron-positron collider PETRA, from 1979 to 1986, at e + ​ e − e^{+}e^{-} annihilation centre-of-mass energies from 12 to 46.7 GeV. The forming of the JADE collaboration, the construction of the apparatus, the most prominent physics highlights, and the post-mortem resurrection and preservation of JADE’s data and software are reviewed.

arxiv-2302-00936.title: Solving Graph Problems Using Gaussian Boson Sampling
arxiv-2302-00936.creator: Yu-Hao Deng, Si-Qiu Gong, Yi-Chao Gu, Zhi-Jiong Zhang, Hua-Liang Liu, Hao Su, Hao-Yang Tang, Jia-Min Xu, Meng-Hao Jia, Ming-Cheng Chen, Han-Sen Zhong, Hui Wang, Jiarong Yan, Yi Hu, Jia Huang, Wei-Jun Zhang, Hao Li, Xiao Jiang, Lixing You, Zhen Wang, Li Li, Nai-Le Liu, Chao-Yang Lu, Jian-Wei Pan
arxiv-2302-00936.description: Abstract Gaussian boson sampling (GBS) is not only a feasible protocol for demonstrating quantum computational advantage, but also mathematically associated with certain graph-related and quantum chemistry problems. In particular, it is proposed that the generated samples from the GBS could be harnessed to enhance the classical stochastic algorithms in searching some graph features.

arxiv-2402-09033.description: Abstract Abstract. Platform businesses operate on a digital core and their decision making requires high-dimensional accurate forecast streams at different levels of cross-sectional (e.g., geographical regions) and temporal aggregation (e.g., minutes to days). It also necessitates coherent forecasts across all levels of the hierarchy to ensure aligned decision making across different planning units such as pricing, product, controlling and strategy.

arxiv-2403-01124.title: Text-guided Explorable Image Super-resolution
arxiv-2403-01124.creator: Kanchana Vaishnavi Gandikota *, Paramanand Chandramouli *
arxiv-2403-01124.description: Abstract In this paper, we introduce the problem of zero-shot text-guided exploration of the solutions to open-domain image super-resolution. Our goal is to allow users to explore diverse, semantically accurate reconstructions that preserve data consistency with the low-resolution inputs for different large downsampling factors without explicitly training for these specific degradations.

In particular, this upper bound is sharp for d = 3 d=3 .

arxiv-2408-16387.description: Abstract This work contributes towards the development of an efficient and scalable open-source Secure Multi-Party Computation (SMPC) protocol on machines with moderate computational resources. We use the ABY2.0 SMPC protocol implemented on the C++ based MOTION2NX framework for secure convolutional neural network (CNN) inference application with semi-honest security. arxiv-2504-10421.title: Can We Edit LLMs for Long-Tail Biomedical Knowledge?
arxiv-2504-10421.creator: Xinhao Yi, Jake Lever, Kevin Bryson, Zaiqiao Meng
arxiv-2504-10421.description: Abstract Knowledge editing has emerged as an effective approach for updating large language models (LLMs) by modifying their internal knowledge. However, their application to the biomedical domain faces unique challenges due to the long-tailed distribution of biomedical knowledge, where rare and infrequent information is prevalent.

arxiv-2508-19372.creator: Zikun Fu, Chen Yang, Kourosh Davoudi, Ken Q. Pu

arxiv-2509-03499.title: DeepSea MOT: A benchmark dataset for multi-object tracking on deep-sea video
arxiv-2509-03499.creator: Kevin Barnard, Elaine Liu, Kristine Walz, Brian Schlining, Nancy Jacobsen Stout, Lonny Lundsten
arxiv-2509-03499.description: Abstract Benchmarking multi-object tracking and object detection model performance is an essential step in machine learning model development, as it allows researchers to evaluate model detection and tracker performance on human-generated ‘test’ data, facilitating consistent comparisons between models and trackers and aiding performance optimization.

arxiv-2511-16498.title: Acquisition Time-Informed Breast Tumor Segmentation from Dynamic Contrast-Enhanced MRI
arxiv-2511-16498.creator: Rui Wang, Yuexi Du, John Lewin, R. Todd Constable, Nicha C. Dvornek
arxiv-2511-16498.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Rui Wang, Yuexi Du, John Lewin, R. Todd Constable, Nicha C. Dvornek. Dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) plays an important role in breast cancer screening, tumor assessment, and treatment planning and monitoring. The dynamic changes in contrast in different tissues help to highlight the tumor in post-contrast images. However, varying acquisition protocols and individual factors result in large variation in the appearance of tissues, even for images acquired in the same phase (e.g., first post-contrast phase), making automated tumor segmentation challenging.

pmc-11646011.title: O072 Sex-based differences in pain perception with short sleep: an experimental study in healthy individuals
pmc-11646011.creator: S Rouhi, N Brumley, A Jordan
pmc-11646011.description: IntroductionExperimental sleep deprivation has been shown to induce pain hypersensitivity, with more pronounced impacts on females than males. However, whether the effect of chronic short sleep on pain perception differs between sexes is unclear. This study investigated the effects of chronic self-reported short sleep (<6 hrs) on pain perception in males and females.

pmc-11716909.title: Comparison of intracranial volume adjustment methods to evaluate brain atrophy severity in AD continuum
pmc-11716909.creator: Wooseok Jung, Chong Hyun Suh, Seung Hyun Lee, Jinyoung Kim, Dong‐Hee Kim, Hyeonwoo Cho, Yeha Lee, Sang Joon Kim
pmc-11716909.description: BackgroundNormative percentile (NP) quantifies brain atrophy by comparing regional brain volumes of a subject against age and sex‐matched cognitively normal populations. Accurate intracranial volume (ICV) adjustment is vital in NP quantification to minimize the effect of an individual’s head size. However, which intracranial volume adjustment method yields reliable normative percentiles remains unclear.

pmc-12563391.title: Comparative Evaluation of Apically Extruded Debris Using Two Rotary and Two Reciprocating File Systems: An In Vitro Study
pmc-12563391.creator: Arjun B Ravi, V. P. Prabath Singh, T. R. Razdan, Shince Mathew, R. Kavitha, Kaushik Haridas
pmc-12563391.description: Aim:The research aimed to quantify, evaluate, and compare the amount of apically extruded debris in 80 extracted mandibular premolars using two rotary and reciprocating file systems.Materials and Method:Rotary and reciprocating single files were employed to instrument root canals. Debris was collected using Eppendorf tubes, and an analytical microbalance was used to ascertain the average weight of debris.

pmc-13485289.creator: Tabish A. Saifee, Keltie O’Neill, Evi Zhuleku, Marco Ghiani, Natasha Dzimitrowicz, Javier Sabater, Jos Becktepe
pmc-13485289.description: IntroductionEssential tremor (ET) carries a substantial burden and unmet need. Limited real-world evidence exists for the epidemiology, clinical characteristics, and treatment patterns of ET in the UK. We conducted a retrospective cohort study using a large electronic health records database from the UK.

pmc-13590257.title: Amphotericin B Colloidal Dispersion Is Effective and Safe for the Treatment of Invasive Aspergillosis in Chinese Patients with Hematologic Disease: A Multicenter, Prospective, Observational, Real-World Study
pmc-13590257.creator: Aiming Pang, Guangxun Gao, Jinhai Ren, Yicheng Zhang, Wei Wang, Rong Fu, Hong Zhang, Bingcheng Liu, Zhangsong Yan, Xiaohui Zheng, Mengnan Lyu, Gang Li, Ying Zhang, Donglin Yang, Sizhou Feng
pmc-13590257.description: PurposeInvasive aspergillosis (IA) causes significant morbidity and mortality in hematologic patients. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety profile of amphotericin B colloidal dispersion (ABCD) for IA in this high-risk population.Patients and MethodsThis multicenter, prospective, observational study enrolled hematologic patients with IA. Eligible patients received ABCD for up to 28 days or until investigator-assessed clinical response or intolerance.

pmc-13627694.title: Handling biological replicates in long-read RNA sequencing data by joining or not joining
pmc-13627694.creator: Fabian Jetzinger, Alejandro Paniagua, Stanley Cormack, Jorge Mestre-Tomás, José Manuel Morante-Redolat, Isabel Fariñas, Luis Ferrández-Peral, Stefan Götz, Carolina Monzó, Ana Conesa
pmc-13627694.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). While isoform identification from long-read RNA sequencing (lrRNA-seq) data has received significant attention, the handling of biologically replicated lrRNA-seq datasets remains less explored. This study defines two strategies for obtaining consensus transcriptomes from multi-sample lrRNA-seq data: Join & Call, where reads from all samples are combined before transcript reconstruction, and Call & Join, where transcript reconstruction is performed on individual samples before combining the resulting annotations.
